title: NOVEMBER BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
Clay County is gearing up to help save lives ahead of the busy holiday season.  The American Red Cross is partnering with local organizations for a series of November blood drives.

First up, Clay Electric Cooperative is sponsoring its fourth annual “giving thanks” drive on Tuesday.  That runs from 1 to 5 pm at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

Then, Flora High School will sponsor a drive on Friday, November 13th.  The high school will host a scholarship-eligible drive in the school gym from 8:30 am until 2 pm.

Finally… A major pre-thanksgiving push is scheduled for Wednesday, November 25th.  Donors can visit the Flora Odd-Fellows Lodge from 1 to 5 pm.

Organizers remind the public that the winter holidays traditionally see a dangerous drop-off in donations.

To be eligible to donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, and weigh at least 110 pounds while in generally good health.  High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger must also meet specific height and weight requirements.  Donors must present a blood donor card, driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

title: TATE’S APPEAL DENIED
full_story:
The Fifth District Appellate Court officially affirmed the natural life sentence of forty-one-year-old Ray E. Tate, ruling there is “no arguable merit” to his attempt to roll back his guilty plea.

Tate pleaded guilty to first-degree murder for the December 2021 shooting of Deputy Sean Riley.  Deputy Riley had responded to what he thought was a routine motorist-assist call on Interstate 64.  Body-worn camera footage captured the sudden ambush, showing Tate drawing a handgun without warning, shooting the deputy in the face, and firing multiple additional rounds.  Tate then dragged the body into a ditch and fled in the deputy’s squad car, sparking a violent, multi-state manhunt and hostage situation.

Following his conviction, Tate attempted to withdraw his plea, claiming he was coerced by jail conditions and arguing that a mandatory life sentence was unconstitutional.

However, the appellate court fiercely rejected those claims, pointing to a mountain of damning evidence.  State records revealed that while awaiting trial, Tate used a jail-provided messaging system to boast about the murder.

Evidence also showed Tate was a severe security risk who meticulously plotted; and nearly executed; a massive jailbreak involving outside accomplices, weapons, and heavy tools smuggled into the facility.

In a sweeping final opinion, the justices noted Tate’s staggering criminal history across multiple states, his total lack of remorse, and the sheer brutality of the crime.  The court ruled that locking Tate away for life does not shock the community’s moral sense, it serves justice.

title: NORTH CLAY REPORT CARD
full_story:
The Illinois State Board of Education officially released its annual report cards, offering a detailed breakdown of academic performance and environment metrics for districts across the state.

For the North Clay School District the Elementary JR High received an approaching exemplary rating and the High School received a Developing rating.

According to the latest 2025-2026 state report card, North Clay District 25 currently operates at an 81.4% financial adequacy level.  On the academic front, the district achieved an overall high school graduation rate of 88.6%.  Student proficiency metrics reveal that 50.3% of students met or exceeded expectations in English Language Arts, while math proficiency across all state tests landed at 29.9%.

On a positive note for the district’s daily student environment, chronic absenteeism remains relatively low at 13.4%.  Officials use these annual report card metrics to evaluate learning standards, track academic growth trends, and map out resource allocation for the upcoming school terms.

title: FREEDOM CAUCUS ON ELECTIONS
full_story:
Tuesday night’s Republican losses in the Illinois House of Representatives continue a trend that began seven years ago under then-Republican Leader Jim Durkin, who has since thrown his support behind Democrat Governor JB Pritzker, according to the Illinois Freedom Caucus.

“In just four presidential cycles, Republicans have declined from 54 seats in the House to an extraordinary low of at least 35 seats after tonight’s results, with several races still undecided.

The question we ask our fellow Republicans is simple; how much worse does it need to get before we try something new?  New people, new ideas, new strategies, and a new direction for Republicans in the General Assembly.

We are ready to unite as Republicans and look to the future, but we cannot ignore failure.  Tonight was an absolute disaster.

We look forward to hearing from our colleagues about their ideas for the future, because the only way to influence change is by winning elections.”

title: CLAY COUNTY RACCOON ROUNDUP
full_story:
The Clay County Farm Bureau is launching a “Raccoon Roundup” program to combat rising property damage from an increased raccoon population.

The initiative offers a $3 cash reward per raccoon tail for Farm Bureau members during the upcoming Illinois hunting and trapping seasons.

Two collection events will take place at the Farm Bureau office in Louisville from 6:00 to 7:00 PM on Thursday, November 12th and January 14th.

Participants are limited to 33 tails per collection date and must present a valid DNR hunting or trapping license.  All harvests must strictly follow state regulations.

title: ISP TO HAVE NITE PATROLS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Captain Bruce Waggoner, announced the ISP will conduct Nighttime Enforcement (NITE) patrols in Marion, Wayne, Effingham, and Hamilton counties this month.  NITE patrols allow the ISP to focus on preventing, detecting, and taking enforcement action in response to impaired driving and occupant restraint violations especially between the hours of 9:00 pm and 6:00 am.

The number of unrestrained drivers killed in traffic crashes is significantly higher at nighttime and combined with impaired driving means even more traffic deaths during these critical hours.

Officers working the enforcement patrols will be watchful for motorists who show signs of impaired driving, improper seatbelt and child restraint usage, speeding, distracted driving, and other Illinois Vehicle Code violations.

Alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be a factor in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  Over half of all fatal crashes in Illinois occur at night.  The NITE program allows officers to work even harder at removing dangerous impaired drivers from the road and making sure everyone is buckled up.

This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: AFBF ON WOTUS
full_story:
The American Farm Bureau Federation is backing proposed changes to the definition of “waters of the US” (WOTUS), saying a supplemental rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency and US Army Corps of Engineers would provide farmers with greater certainty about which water features fall under federal Clean Water Act jurisdiction.

In comments submitted earlier this month, AFBF said the proposal aligns with the US Supreme Court’s 2023 Sackett v. EPA decision and could help end years of uncertainty surrounding WOTUS regulations.

“Farmers and ranchers support the supplemental rule because it brings Clean Water Act jurisdiction in line with Sackett and the statute’s text, and it gives farm families the clarity and stability they have sought for decades,” the organization wrote.

The supplemental proposal published in September follows a 2025 rulemaking that defined federally regulated waters as those considered “relatively permanent,” including waters that flow year-round or during a state’s “wet season.”  After receiving public comments, the agencies proposed replacing the “wet season” standard with a requirement that covered waters be “perennial,” meaning they contain standing or continuously flowing water every day of the year under ordinary conditions.  The proposal seeks comments on the revised definitions of “relatively permanent” and continuous surface connection.”

The organization said the proposal’s focus on relatively permanent waters and wetlands with a continuous surface connection reflects the standards established in Sackett and would provide farmers with a more observable, predictable framework.

Farm Bureau also urged regulators to retain specific exclusions for agricultural drainage and irrigation ditches, prior converted cropland and similar features.  Without a clear ditch exemption, the group warned that some farm drainage systems could be considered federal waters.

While supporting the proposal, AFBF said implementation details remain important.  The organization urged agencies to base jurisdictional decisions on actual field conditions rather than maps or models and said regulators should bear the burden of proving federal jurisdiction.
